context: Linked parallel coordinates + world map explorer for 40 cities across 6 dimensions (population, density, elevation, temp, rainfall, cost index); brushing the parallel coords filters cities highlighted on the map.
first_impression: Structurally honest parallel coordinates visualization with data-driven scale domains and a well-implemented linked selection model.
what_works: Scale domains use d3.extent() + .nice() throughout — no hardcoded magic numbers. Axis scales are fixed at initial extent and do not recalculate on filter, preventing axis-jumping under the subset metamorphic relation.
what_doesnt: No key function in the SVG city dot join (.data(cities).join('circle')) — benign with static data but would corrupt identity under permutation if data were ever updated. City dot radius on the map is hardcoded (3px unselected, 4px selected) rather than data-driven, but this is a categorical distinction, not an encoding violation.
